---
title: "Interventions and nets"
---

```{python}
#| include: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.style.use("styles/mint.mplstyle")
```

MINTverse models three vector-control levers, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs), indoor
residual spraying (IRS), and larval source management (LSM). Nets carry most of the detail.
A net choice and a resistance level are reduced to a single lethality number before either
package will look at them.

## Net types

ITNs are grouped into four formulations. Their names are the keyword arguments to
`calculate_dn0` and `Scenario`, and they are the allowed values of `net_type_future`.

| Name | Formulation | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `py_only` | Pyrethroid only | The baseline net |
| `py_pbo` | Pyrethroid with PBO | Restores kill in resistant populations |
| `py_pyrrole` | Pyrethroid with a pyrrole (chlorfenapyr) | Kill that does not decay with pyrethroid resistance |
| `py_ppf` | Pyrethroid with pyriproxyfen (PPF) | An effect on the next generation, folded into `lsm` |

The long forms are the canonical values. `net_types()` returns them alphabetically, which
puts `ppf` before `pyrrole`, so indexing into the list rather than naming the net is a
common source of error.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from estimint import calculate_dn0, net_types

net_types()
```

The short aliases are accepted everywhere the long forms are.

## Net effectiveness and dn0

A net's effect on transmission is summarised by `dn0`, the probability that a mosquito is
killed when it contacts a treated net. The value depends on the insecticide and on the local
level of pyrethroid resistance, and `calculate_dn0` takes those two things, a resistance
level and a net mix, and returns the usage-weighted `dn0` along with the total coverage.

```{python}
mix = calculate_dn0(0.5, py_only=0.4, py_pbo=0.2)
mix
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## `itn_use` is already the total coverage

`DN0Result.itn_use` is the **sum of the shares you passed**, which here is 0.4 + 0.2 =
0.6. It is not a scaling factor waiting to be applied. Multiplying it by a usage figure a
second time halves the coverage, which lowers the modelled protection and raises the EIR
the setting is judged to need. No warning is issued.
:::

## Resistance response

We set usage to 1.0 for one net type at a time and sweep resistance from 0 to 1, which gives
the resistance response of each formulation on its own terms.

```{python}
nets = ["py_only", "py_pbo", "py_pyrrole", "py_ppf"]
resistance = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 41)

dn0 = pd.DataFrame(
    {net: [calculate_dn0(r, **{net: 1.0}).dn0 for r in resistance] for net in nets},
    index=pd.Index(resistance, name="resistance"),
)

dn0.loc[[0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]].round(4)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Probability a mosquito dies on contact with a net (`dn0`), against pyrethroid resistance, for each net type at full usage."
#| fig-alt: "Four declining curves of dn0 against resistance from 0 to 1. The amber pyrrole curve is highest throughout, starting near 0.56 and staying flattest before falling away past 0.75. The green PBO curve starts near 0.51 and the purple PPF curve near 0.41, and the two converge at high resistance and cross at about 0.92, after which purple is the higher. The blue pyrethroid-only curve is lowest throughout, starting near 0.34 and falling to zero at full resistance."
fig, ax = plt.subplots()

for net in nets:
    ax.plot(dn0.index, dn0[net], label=net)

ax.set_xlabel("Pyrethroid resistance")
ax.set_ylabel("dn0 (probability of death on contact)")
ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
ax.set_ylim(0, None)
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

Notice that the highest and the lowest curve never change places, and that the gap between
them widens as resistance rises. The amber pyrrole curve sits above the other three at every
resistance level and the blue pyrethroid-only curve below them all, and the ratio between the
two grows from about 1.7 at zero resistance to about 2.5 at 0.9. This is because
chlorfenapyr kills through a pathway that pyrethroid resistance does not act on, so the amber
curve gives up only the pyrethroid share of its lethality. The blue curve has nothing else to
give up. It reaches zero when resistance is total.

Notice also the green PBO curve and the purple PPF curve crossing at about 0.92, and the
sharp fall in all four curves beyond 0.75. Green runs above purple almost everywhere. Only in
the last few hundredths does purple come out ahead. This is because PBO works by restoring
the kill of the pyrethroid itself, and there is nothing left to restore once resistance is
near total, while PPF carries a component that survives it.

The resistance-to-`dn0` curves come from the same published source that `malariasimulation`
uses. They are a lookup table rather than a fitted model.

## IRS and LSM

IRS and LSM enter as coverage proportions. `irs_use` is the spraying coverage in place now,
`irs_future` the coverage under the campaign being evaluated, and `lsm` the larval term, all
on a 0 to 1 scale. Neither has a `dn0`-style effectiveness term, so the coverage itself is
the input.

PPF nets feed into the LSM term. `run_scenarios` folds PPF coverage into `lsm` before the
emulator runs, at a factor of 0.248. The factor is not configurable.

$$
\texttt{lsm\_eff} = \min\big(\texttt{py\_ppf} \times 0.248 + \texttt{lsm},\ 1.0\big)
$$

So a scenario with PPF nets at 0.5 coverage and LSM at 0.30 reaches the emulator with an
effective LSM of $0.5 \times 0.248 + 0.30 = 0.424$.

::: {.callout-important}
## The `lsm` column is `lsm_eff`

The `lsm` column in the `run_scenarios` output is reported after the PPF contribution has
been added, so it is not the `lsm` you passed. If you are reconciling a scenario's inputs
against its outputs, or diffing two scenarios, this is the column that will not match.
:::

## Limitations of dn0

`dn0` summarises the probability of death on contact, and nothing else. Repellence is not in
it. Neither the protection that repellence gives nor the diversion of biting it produces is
anywhere in the number.

Nor does it capture attrition. A net mix is a snapshot at the decision point, and `dn0` and
`itn_use` are held constant across the trajectory, so a campaign's protection arrives in full
at day 3285 and holds.

A single mix covers the whole population. A district where half the villages have new nets
and half have five-year-old nets is not a district uniformly in the middle, but it will be
represented as one.

Note that a setting above 0.75 resistance sits in the steep part of every curve, where a
small error in the resistance level supplied produces a large error in `dn0`. Vary it in a
sensitivity check rather than trusting a single value.
